encodedUser.description: Encoded (raw) user of URL, ex. user = 'c3iot'.

encodedPassword.description: Encoded (raw) raw password of URL, ex. password = 'pwd'.

port.description: Port Number of URL, ex. port = 8080. Will null if missing.

encodedQuery.description: Encoded (raw) query of URL (after the `?` mark), ex. 'ion=1&espv=8'. (This will not include the fragment.)

encodedFragment.description: Encoded (raw) fragment of URL (after the `#` mark), ex. 'chapter1'.

title:
Type for parsing and constructing Uniform Resource Locator (URL) strings.

Consider the example URL `ftp://c3iot:pwd@ftp.example.com:8080/docs/my%20resource.html?ion=1&espv=8#chapter1`:
- {@link #scheme scheme}: "ftp"
- {@link #encodedUser encodedUser}: "c3iot"
- {@link #encodedPassword encodedPassword}: "pwd"
- {@link #host host}: "ftp.example.com"
- {@link #port port}: 8080
- {@link #encodedPath encodedPath}: "/docs/my%20resource.html"
- {@link #encodedQuery encodedQuery}: "ion=1&espv=8"
- {@link #encodedFragment encodedFragment}: "chapter1"

All fields prefixed with "encoded" will have special characters encoded. Corresponding methods without "encoded"
will use {@link UrlEncoder#decodePathComponent} to produce the raw value. For example "my%20resource.html" is
encoding a space as "%20" and the {@link #path path} method will return "my resource.html".

@see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/Common_questions/Web_mechanics/What_is_a_URL
name: Url
